Grim Tarn.narrative: I've fished the west shore since I could hold a line, and the salt pans behind me were my father's and his father's before him. That channel at the north end is ours by right of two generations, and I'll not have Hollis Brine pushing his traps into it and calling it free water. My boat hook was stolen by the Coldwell outlaws last winter, and I've not forgotten it. Nessa is courting a Brine boy, and while the debt to Rook Tarn stands unpaid, I'll not have him at my table.
goals: keep the north channel for my traps
see the debt to Rook Tarn settled
protect my daughter from a match I distrust
keep the salt pans working through winter
learn to read the weather off the western sky better than any neighbour
see the salt pans pass to someone who will keep them working

memories.gist: My father showed me the north channel and said, 'This is ours, boy, as long as the Tarns fish it.'
The Lean Year: we ate salt fish and thin barley, and the wolves came down to the shore.
Hollis Brine moved his traps into the channel last spring, and I told him to move them back.
The Coldwell outlaws took my boat hook from the shed; I found the shed door broken.
Nessa told me she was walking out with Tarn Brine, and I told her not while the debt stands.

stances.why: The channel has been Tarn water for two generations.
They take what isn't theirs and don't pay their debts.
Blood is what holds the shore together.
A man who doesn't pay his debts is no better than an outlaw.
They stole from me once; they'll do it again if they can.

sitting at the pans at dusk watching the salt form
Grim Tarn.calling: I fish the west shore and work the salt pans my father left me, and that is the work I want and mean to keep.

Ebba Tarn.narrative: I work the salt pans and keep the goats and the herb plot, and I've set bones and dosed coughs for half the saltings. The Brines come to me when the cough takes them, and I treat them the same as anyone. I've no quarrel with Marra, but I'll not cross my husband in front of them. The winter store worries me, and the wolves come closer each year.

see Nessa happy without breaking the household
keep the herb plot and the medicines stocked
avoid open quarrel with the Brines
grow a fuller herb plot and learn a cure she does not yet know
see Nessa settled happily in a house of her own

memories.gist: My mother taught me the herb plot and the salt pans, and said, 'Heal who you can, and don't judge.'
The Surge: we lost a boat and nearly lost Grim; the sea took the lower shore.
I dosed Marra Brine's cough last winter, and she thanked me kindly.
Grim told Nessa she couldn't see Tarn Brine, and she cried in the goat shed.
The wolves came down to the saltings and took a goat; I heard them in the dark.

stances.why: A healer doesn't turn away the sick, whatever the quarrel.
The household is what keeps us through winter.
I won't defy Grim in front of the Brines, but I'll not make enemies either.
The store must last; the wolves and the cold don't wait.
I told Grim to leave Nessa and Tarn alone; they'll sort it themselves.

Ebba Tarn.calling: I set bones and dose coughs for the saltings, and I would have my medicines better stocked and my hands surer at it.

Nessa Tarn.narrative: I help my mother with the pans and the goats and my father with the boat, and I'm a fair hand with a spear. I like Tarn Brine, and I'm angry with my father for using the debt as a gate. I meet Tarn on the shore when I can, but I'm afraid of the deep water beyond the shore and I dream of seeing Lanternquay and the tide lanterns.
goals: see Tarn Brine without my father's leave
visit Lanternquay and see the tide lanterns
keep the goats and pans well
become a truly good hand with the spear

memories.gist: I speared my first big fish last summer, and Father clapped me on the back.
Tarn Brine gave me a shell from the north shore, and I keep it under my pillow.
Father said Tarn couldn't come to the house until the debt is settled, and I shouted at him.
I saw the tide lanterns at Lanternquay from the cliff once, and I've wanted to go ever since.

stances.why: He's kind and I want to be with him, whatever Father says.
I love my parents, but they're wrong about this.
There's more than the saltings, and I want to see it.
The sea beyond the shore is dark and cold, and I've heard stories.

Nessa Tarn.calling: I work the pans and goats and the boat with my family, but the work I long for is out on the water with a spear, and one day on a bigger water than this shore.
